title: IB ESS Extended Response: A High-Mark Method
summary: IB ESS extended response strategy for decoding prompts, planning in two minutes, building balanced arguments and checking answers under exam pressure.
body_markdown:
An **IB ESS extended response** asks you to turn knowledge into a reasoned answer: decode the command term, select relevant evidence, explain mechanisms and reach a justified judgement. A reliable method is to plan briefly, give each paragraph one analytical purpose and evaluate throughout.


Recognising a topic can make writing feel urgent. But knowing about biodiversity is different from judging whether a particular conservation strategy works. That distinction should guide your response.


Before writing, check:


- What does the command term require?
- What limits the question’s scope?
- Which arguments and examples support a judgement?
- What conditions might change your conclusion?


The ESS course first assessed in 2026 includes short-answer, data-based and extended-response work in Paper 2. See the[guide to ESS assessment](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-is-ess-assessed-in-the-new-syllabus-2026-first-assessment) for the wider format.


### Decode the question before answering


Identify three layers: **command term, subject and scope** . Scope may restrict your answer to a location, stakeholder, strategy or environmental value system.


Consider a hypothetical question asking whether protected areas are the most effective way to conserve biodiversity. Describing protected areas answers only part of it. You must assess their effectiveness, consider limitations, compare plausible alternatives and judge “most effective.”


Command term Required approach


Explain Connect causes, processes or consequences to show how or why.


Discuss Review different arguments, evidence or perspectives in balance.


Evaluate Weigh strengths and limitations, then reach a judgement.


Justify Support a position with evidence and reasoning.


To what extent Judge how far a claim holds, including exceptions.


Practise these distinctions with the[guide to common ESS command terms](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-command-terms-are-most-common-in-ess-exams-2026-first-assessment) .
